claims.statement: As verified on 2026-07-19, the VetMedAI knowledge base holds about 31 content documents in `knowledge/`, which is 34 Markdown files when the README is counted, below the paper's figure of 41. Checked against the deliverable on 2026-07-25, no knowledge document count is reported there any longer; the claim stands as a checked finding about the repository.

claims.title: Empirical review finds vibe coding fast and accessible but perceived as unreliable, a speed-quality trade-off.
claims.statement: A systematic grey-literature review of practitioner accounts finds that vibe coding is motivated by speed and accessibility yet yields code its own practitioners perceive as fast but flawed, lowering barriers at the cost of reliability and maintainability. This is the empirical support for the paper's Section 2.4 positioning, where Promptotyping shares the generation premise of vibe coding but adds preparation, persistent documentation and verification.

claims.title: Sacha's knowledge generation model describes the visual-analytics process by integrating existing frameworks.
claims.statement: Sacha and colleagues propose a knowledge generation model that ties together diverse visual-analytics frameworks and gives a high-level description of the human and computer processes inside such systems. This grounds the paper's Section 4.2 use of the model as the process framework that comes closest to an epistemic account of visual analytics, yet describes the process rather than classifying interfaces by the epistemic function they serve.

claims.title: Visualisation in the humanities is a research process in its own right, not merely an instrument serving research.
claims.statement: Hinrichs, Forlini and Moynihan introduce the sandcastle to reframe visualisation as a research process in its own right, against the predominant DH terminology of prototypes and tools that casts visualisations as a means to an end in the service of humanities research.

claims.title: Provenance and the interests a dataset encodes remain the scholar's responsibility; well-modelled data does not discharge critical data work.
claims.statement: Because data emerges from structures of power and reflects societal hierarchies, the critical examination of how a dataset came to be, its provenance, who made its metadata, and whose interests it serves, remains the scholar's responsibility, and the AI turn makes this critical data work more rather than less crucial. This grounds the paper's Section 6.4 limit: FAIR-grade, well-modelled data eases generation but does not relieve the scholar of interrogating the data's origin and encoded interests.

claims.title: Wheaton's stated Section 5 figures held against the repository as verified on 2026-07-19.
claims.statement: The Wheaton case study's stated figures, 1,124 transactions and 718 individuals, matched the project repository when the Section 5 verification checked them on 2026-07-19. Checked against the deliverable on 2026-07-25, neither figure is reported there any longer; the deliverable names the Wheaton Day Book without counts. The claim stands as a checked finding about the repository.

claims.title: Community-curated tool registries on Wikidata answer the directory paradox by treating tool data as a maintained commons.
claims.statement: Grallert et al. argue that curated tool directories inevitably go stale in fast-moving fields (the directory paradox), and propose open, community-curated registries that act as authority files and knowledge bases of a field's methodological practices, with Wikidata as the data store positioning tool data as part of the commons. This is the registry infrastructure the paper points to for the findability of small generated instruments.

claims.title: The ZBZ repository shows 305 commits spanning 2026-01-29 to 2026-07-09 as verified on 2026-07-19.
claims.statement: As verified on 2026-07-19, the ZBZ repository shows 305 commits spanning 2026-01-29 to 2026-07-09, a wider range than the paper's 128 commits over six weeks. Checked against the deliverable on 2026-07-25, no commit count is reported there any longer; the claim stands as a checked finding about the repository.

claims.title: ZBZ's stated Section 5 volume figures held against the repository as verified on 2026-07-19.
claims.statement: The ZBZ case study's stated volume figures held against the project repository when the Section 5 verification checked them on 2026-07-19, covering 286 PDFs, about 4,150 pages at an actual 4,117, and more than 30 Python scripts at an actual 98. Checked against the deliverable on 2026-07-25, the 286 PDFs and the approximately 4,150 pages are still reported there, while the script count is not; for that figure the claim stands as a checked finding about the repository.

claims.title: The ZBZ knowledge base holds 13 content documents plus an index as verified on 2026-07-19.
claims.statement: As verified on 2026-07-19, the ZBZ knowledge base holds 13 content documents plus an index, and the 3 Action Documents the paper names were not found in the repository. Checked against the deliverable on 2026-07-25, neither a knowledge document count nor the Action Documents are reported there any longer; the claim stands as a checked finding about the repository.
